name: OrderUp Retail
author: orderupmt

sections.description:
OrderUp Retail connects a WooCommerce shop to OrderUp, which lists the shop’s products on Wolt Retail and Bolt Market.

  • OrderUp reads your published products: names, descriptions, SKUs, barcodes (GTIN, UPC, EAN or ISBN), prices (including tax), stock, images, categories, tags and attributes. Variable products come through as one record per variation.
  • When you edit a product or its stock changes, the plugin tells OrderUp within about 30 seconds, so Wolt Retail and Bolt Market show the change quickly. OrderUp also re-reads the whole catalogue every 15 minutes.
  • The plugin only reads. It never changes your products, orders or settings.
  • Only OrderUp can read the catalogue: every request must carry your shop’s connection token.

You need an OrderUp account to use this plugin. The connection token comes from the OrderUp portal.

External services

This plugin connects your shop to OrderUp, a service run by OrderUp (https://orderup.mt) that lists your products on Wolt Retail and Bolt Market. It does nothing until you paste an OrderUp connection token on its settings page.

What OrderUp reads from your shop. OrderUp calls the plugin’s REST endpoint (/wp-json/orderup/v1/catalogue) about every 15 minutes, and straight after a change notice. It sends your connection token with each call. It reads your published products and variations: name, description, SKU, barcode (WooCommerce’s GTIN, UPC, EAN or ISBN field), price and regular price (including tax), stock status and quantity, image URLs, product categories, product tags, and the attributes shown on the product page or used for variations (such as size or colour). It reads no customer, order or user data.

What the plugin sends to OrderUp. When a product is created, edited, trashed or deleted, or its stock changes, the plugin waits 30 seconds and then sends the ids of the changed products to OrderUp’s server (retail.orderup.mt), with your connection token. Nothing else is sent.

  • OrderUp terms of service: https://orderup.mt/terms/
  • OrderUp privacy policy: https://orderup.mt/privacy-policy/
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. Install OrderUp Retail from Plugins › Add New, or upload the orderup-retail folder to /wp-content/plugins/, and activate it.
  3. In the OrderUp portal, open Menus › Feeds › Website and copy the connection token.
  4. In WordPress, go to WooCommerce › OrderUp Retail, paste the token and click Save token.
sections.faq:
Do I need an OrderUp account?

Yes. The plugin only shares your catalogue with OrderUp, and OrderUp lists it on Wolt Retail and Bolt Market. Contact OrderUp at https://orderup.mt to get set up.

Does the plugin change anything in my shop?

No. It only reads products, prices, stock, images, categories, tags and attributes. Orders from Wolt and Bolt are handled by OrderUp, not written into WooCommerce by this plugin.

Which prices are sent?

The price the customer pays, including tax, as WooCommerce calculates it. A product on sale shows both the sale price and the regular price.

My server runs no WP-Cron. Will change notices still go out?

Change notices are sent by a WP-Cron event. If WP-Cron is disabled and no system cron runs it, the notices wait, but OrderUp’s full read every 15 minutes still picks up every change.

What happens when I delete the plugin?

Its settings (the token and the last change notice) are removed.
sections.changelog:
1.2.0

  • Each product now includes its tags, and its attributes (the ones shown on the product page or used for variations). A variation gets its own value, such as its size or colour.

1.1.1

  • The full catalogue leaves out products with no SKU of their own, or with tracked stock below zero, until they are fixed. A change notice still sends them, so a product that drops below zero is marked sold out straight away.
  • The plugin description and settings page now name both Wolt Retail and Bolt Market.

1.1.0

  • Licensed GPLv2 or later, for the WordPress.org plugin directory.
  • Translatable settings page, and a Settings link on the Plugins screen.
  • Deleting the plugin now removes its settings.
  • Each product now includes its barcode from WooCommerce’s GTIN, UPC, EAN or ISBN field (WooCommerce 9.2 or later), so Wolt Retail and Bolt Market can match it.
  • No change to the change notices.

1.0.1

  • An ids= filter with no valid id now returns nothing instead of the whole catalogue.
  • The settings page says why a token was rejected, and confirms when it is saved.

1.0.0

  • First release.
